identity.label: Scene sequel structure
identity.summary: Story-development skill for diagnosing and designing scene chains through goal, conflict, disaster, reaction, dilemma, decision, half-scene handling, and next-goal handoff.

memory_routing: Use for author-support scene diagnosis, revision, outline chaining, and prompt-pack scaffolding rather than direct live-scene control.
Route active scene goal, owner, scene question, obstacle, disaster/outcome, aftermath, decision, and next scene goal to Scenario Book.
Route recurring goal style, reaction style, dilemma habits, and decision patterns to Character Book when the author saves them.
Route meaningful disasters, hollow victories, injuries, mistakes, decisions, unresolved consequences, and new commitments to Memory Book.

guardrails: Do not force every scene into a visible worksheet or rigid formula.
Do not invent random disasters; outcomes should grow from the goal and conflict.
Do not skip reaction, dilemma, and decision when a setback needs emotional or practical processing.
Do not make every disaster maximum intensity; scale to genre, arc position, scene purpose, and reader promise.
Preserve {{user}} agency and author control over canon, tone, point of view, and final revision choices.
